_comment: Enrollment for historic play (§10.1 lifecycle, §14 simplified), Phase 1 checkpoint 1h: one intake a year at move-in, graduation and year changes at commencement, attrition from the §32 retention formula (balance.json retention), faculty hired to a student/faculty ratio. Admissions proper (marketing, yield, aid) come later. All numbers are [TWEAK] placeholders, not history.
_assumed_gpa_comment: GPA isn't simulated yet (learning model, §13.5); the retention formula uses this.
_eras_comment: Per era id (eras.json); 'default' covers eras not listed. applicants = applicants_per_year x applicant_growth_per_year^(years since the scenario start).

founding._balance_comment: Chapter 1 balance pass (2026-10-02, tools/BalanceRunner): 12 students per professor hired $600 of salary for every $240 of tuition, so each new student lost money and even an idle game was dismissed by 1835. At 25 a student roughly pays for their share of a professor (the sources point to about 33: 234 students and 7 professors in 1834, events/old_miami_1834.json). Applicant growth 8% -> 6% a year, because Reputation (reputation.json) now adds applicants for a well-run college [TWEAK].
founding._class_comment: The 1824 college day per Upham, Old Miami (1909): rise before 5, study 5-7 and 2-5, recitations 7-8 and 9-12, prayers in the evening; a required 6 a.m. chapel per Wikipedia's Sesquicentennial Chapel article. Saturday classes are an assumption (common in early colleges) [VERIFY].

town_boarding._comment: Students who can't live in a university hall board with families in town (§18.3 grows into the off-campus market later). Beds per town-land tile within max_distance_m of the campus.

_default_capacity_comment: Capacity of real buildings whose timeline entry has no building_def (seats for academic buildings, beds for residences ...).

scholarship._comment: §13.7 minimal: each faculty member produces research_score/100 x works_per_year scholarly works a year (publications, sermons, lectures in print ...), tallied at commencement.
